rows.name: Constellation Software Inc.
rows.last_memo: Constellation's stock jumped about 6.5% today with no apparent reason — no earnings, no acquisition news, no management update. For a company like this, where what matters is whether management keeps buying good software businesses at attractive prices and compounding free cash f

rows.name: Deckers Outdoor Corp.
rows.last_memo: Deckers had a decent but not exceptional quarter—sales grew about 6%, the direct-to-consumer business (selling straight to shoppers, bypassing retailers) grew a healthy 13%, and international demand kept building. The downside is that spending on overhead and marketing grew much
risks: SG&A growing at 2.2x the rate of revenue in Q1 FY27; if this reflects a higher-cost operating model rather than investment spending, operating margins could structurally compress by 200-300bps versus thesis assumptions.

Inventory rose $320M in the quarter to $807.6M—a seasonal build but the absolute level warrants monitoring against sell-through data; any buildup into fiscal year-end would be a kill-criterion proximity signal.

Operating lease commitments surged ($120M of new ROU assets in one quarter vs. $45M prior year), indicating a significant retail or distribution footprint expansion; lease costs are fixed obligations that increase operating leverage in a downturn.
Tariff uncertainty explicitly mentioned in forward-looking statements; as a footwear company with overseas manufacturing, any sustained tariff escalation could structurally raise COGS.

rows.name: Meta Platforms Inc.
rows.last_memo: Zuckerberg wrote a very long public essay about his vision to make advanced AI available to everyone, leaning into Meta's open-source strategy. This is consistent with what Meta has been doing for the past two years with its Llama AI models and heavy infrastructure spending — it'
risks: If the 'superintelligent AI for everyone' framing accelerates capex commitments beyond current guidance without a clear monetization bridge, it could pressure FCF margins sooner than the thesis anticipates — but this is a latent risk, not a confirmed one from this event.

Open-source AI model leadership could inadvertently lower barriers for competitors (including smaller ad-tech players) to build targeting capabilities, potentially eroding Meta's AI-driven advertising edge over a 5-10 year horizon.
Mandated teen-protection product overhauls may restrict ad load and data collection on under-18 users across Facebook and Instagram, creating a measurable but currently unquantified revenue drag.

New Mexico ruling may embolden other U.S. states or federal regulators to pursue similar child safety actions, creating a patchwork of compliance obligations that raises operating complexity and cost.

rows.name: International Business Machines Corporation
rows.last_memo: IBM just got permission to sell its Maximo software — which helps large organizations manage buildings, equipment, and physical assets — to U.S. federal government agencies. Previously, a missing government security certification blocked these sales entirely. This is genuinely go
risks: Federal procurement cycles are notoriously slow; FedRAMP authorization may not translate to meaningful revenue for 2-3 years, creating an execution timing gap.
Competing asset management vendors (ServiceNow, Oracle, SAP) may also pursue or already hold FedRAMP certifications, limiting IBM's first-mover window.

If the top-line miss reflects software or Red Hat deceleration rather than consulting/infrastructure, the primary growth engine of the thesis is impaired — this must be confirmed or ruled out via segment data.
Net debt/EBITDA at 3.47x remains above the 2.5x discipline threshold; any FCF guidance reduction would tighten this constraint materially.

rows.name: Amazon Com Inc.
rows.last_memo: Amazon's cloud boss said that essentially all of their AI server capacity is already committed to customers through 2028 — think of it like a hotel where every room is booked years in advance. This is important because one of the biggest questions about Amazon has been whether co
risks: Execution risk on supply side: if Amazon cannot build data center and AI chip capacity fast enough to honor multi-year commitments, customer satisfaction and contract terms could be impaired.

Concentration risk: capacity locked through 2028 means AWS is betting heavily on AI workloads remaining on current architectural assumptions — a disruptive shift in AI compute paradigm (e.g., dramatically more efficient models) could strand infrastructure investment.
Memory price inflation adding ~$20B to the capex program creates a near-term FCF headwind that could persist through 2026-2027 depending on DRAM/HBM market conditions.

Long-term debt doubled from $65.6B to $128.9B in six months (H1 2026 new issuance of ~$67B); while net debt/EBITDA remains well below 2.5x given earnings scale, the leverage trajectory warrants monitoring.

rows.name: Microsoft Corporation
rows.last_memo: Two news articles appeared about Microsoft — one noting an analyst changed their 2027 price target, another ranking Microsoft against Amazon and Google in cloud. Neither article gave us any actual numbers, reasoning, or new facts about Microsoft's business. They are headlines wit
risks: Unknown AI strategic decision may affect Copilot pricing, partnership structure, or product roadmap — cannot quantify until details are available.
If the 'controversial decision' relates to OpenAI partnership terms or exclusivity arrangements, it could affect Azure AI differentiation — requires verification.

If AI-specific package targeting escalates, enterprise customers may impose stricter controls on open-source dependencies, marginally slowing developer adoption of Microsoft AI tooling on GitHub/Azure.

Repeated supply-chain incidents on npm could provide competitive ammunition for GitLab, JFrog Artifactory, or other alternative artifact registries seeking to displace GitHub in enterprise environments.

rows.name: Alphabet Inc.
rows.last_memo: Alphabet just borrowed $25 billion by issuing bonds to investors, which is notable because this company usually sits on a massive pile of cash and rarely needs to borrow. The bonds range from short-term (due 2028) to very long-term (due 2066), at interest rates between roughly 4.
risks: Use of proceeds is undisclosed; a large acquisition at a full multiple would represent a capital discipline risk inconsistent with the thesis.
If debt is used to fund buybacks at 24x forward earnings, management is prioritizing financial engineering over reinvestment, which would be a credibility yellow flag.
Long-dated tranches (40-year notes at 6.5%) lock in financing cost at elevated rates; if AI capex returns disappoint, this leverage becomes harder to justify.
If AI infrastructure returns disappoint, Alphabet will have permanently increased its capital base and interest burden with limited ability to quickly reverse the commitment.

rows.name: NVIDIA Corporation
rows.last_memo: Countries around the world are starting to spend serious money building their own national AI computing infrastructure rather than relying solely on big tech clouds — think of it like each country wanting its own AI 'power grid.' NVIDIA is the most obvious beneficiary because its
risks: Sovereign AI demand is disproportionately concentrated in regions (Middle East, Southeast Asia, parts of Europe) where U.S. export controls could restrict NVIDIA's ability to deliver H100/B200-class hardware, potentially capping addressable sovereign TAM.
Government procurement cycles are slower and more unpredictable than hyperscaler capex, introducing potential lumpiness in recognized revenue if this channel grows.
Vendor financing of GPU purchases, if confirmed and material, introduces credit concentration risk to NVIDIA's balance sheet tied to OpenAI's financial health.
A pattern of vendor-financed demand would raise questions about whether AI infrastructure capex is as organically robust as current revenue growth implies.

rows.name: Palantir Tech Inc.
rows.last_memo: Palantir's business is doing well — revenue is growing fast, it generates real cash, and its software is becoming more embedded in how large organizations and governments make decisions. The CEO publicly warned that companies are wasting money on AI that doesn't actually work, po
risks: Karp's public AI warning, while strategically smart, could signal that enterprise AI deployment timelines are stretching, which would delay AIP revenue conversion from bootcamps and pilots to large multi-year contracts.

At 68x trailing sales and ~155x EV/EBITDA, the stock is priced for perfection across a decade — any macro shock, competitor breakthrough, or government budget sequester that interrupts the growth trajectory could cause severe price correction even without fundamental business damage.

Hyperscaler AI platforms (Microsoft Copilot for enterprise, AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex AI) are maturing rapidly and may offer 'good enough' orchestration at zero marginal cost for existing cloud customers, pressuring Palantir's commercial win rates over time.

At $172/share (~$413B market cap, ~67x TTM revenue, ~152x EV/EBITDA), the stock now prices in a near-perfect multi-decade execution scenario, leaving almost no margin for error and making position-sizing discipline essential.

rows.name: Shopify Inc.
rows.last_memo: Shopify reported a better-than-expected quarter with strong sales growth and solid profit, driven by merchants processing more transactions through the platform. The company is also leaning hard into AI as a way to make its tools more powerful for merchants, which is a smart defe
risks: AI commerce strategy adds execution risk: if Shopify is investing heavily in AI tooling to stay ahead, this may pressure near-term margins or require capital allocation that delays FCF margin expansion.

AI-native commerce platforms (e.g., those building directly on LLM infrastructure) could bypass traditional storefront software entirely — the Q2 call highlights this is on management's radar, suggesting competitive intensity is real.
Valuation-to-fair-value gap (current price ~16x base case fair value) means any miss or guidance cut would cause severe price dislocations, even if the long-term thesis remains intact.
A 17% single-day move compresses the margin of safety further on an already premium valuation, making the stock more sensitive to any future guidance miss.

rows.name: Unitedhealth Group Inc.
rows.last_memo: UnitedHealth's most recent quarter shows the company's core insurance business is healing — it spent about $3 billion less on medical claims in the first half of 2026 compared to the same period last year, while collecting roughly the same premiums. That's the financial equivalen
risks: Senator Warren's break-up push, if it gains political momentum during an election cycle, could accelerate regulatory scrutiny of UNH's vertical integration, even absent immediate legislative action.
Operating costs (non-medical) grew $2.3B YoY in H1 2026 — if this reflects structural cost creep in Optum rather than investment for growth, it could offset MCR gains.

Loss on sale of subsidiaries ($133M in H1 2026) and held-for-sale disclosures suggest asset dispositions are ongoing; unclear whether divestitures are value-accretive or forced by regulatory pressure.
Medicare Part D plan economics worsen materially in 2027 if UNH cannot reprice premiums fast enough to offset subsidy loss, pressuring both insurance and Optum pharmacy margins simultaneously.

rows.name: Tesla Inc.
rows.last_memo: A well-known NFL coach was in a car crash where Tesla's Autopilot may have been active, putting the company back under a media spotlight on safety. This isn't the first time Tesla has faced this kind of scrutiny, and one crash alone won't derail the autonomous driving program. Bu
risks: Formal NHTSA or NTSB investigation triggered by the Shanahan incident could impose interim operational restrictions on Autopilot deployment or require software modifications.
Congressional or state-level legislative action using this incident as political catalyst to tighten autonomous vehicle regulations, potentially delaying robotaxi licensing timelines.
Consumer confidence erosion in FSD subscriptions dampens near-term attach rates and recurring software revenue growth.
Plaintiffs' bar acceleration: a high-profile incident with a public figure increases likelihood of civil litigation that sets adverse legal precedent for autonomous liability.

rows.name: AST SpaceMobile Inc.
rows.last_memo: AST SpaceMobile is finally generating real revenue — about $31.5 million in the second quarter of 2026, up from basically nothing a year ago — which shows that phone carriers are actually paying for their services. But buried in the financial results is a $126 million charge for
risks: Satellite involuntary conversion loss of $125.9M in Q2 2026 signals an operational failure event whose root cause, scope, and insurance recovery remain undisclosed — this is the single most important new risk.

Long-term debt has reached $3.0B (up $756M in six months) with another convertible note issued in July 2026; the capital structure is becoming complex and interest expense ($50M H1) is material relative to revenue ($46M H1).

Revenue mix is heavily weighted to low-margin gateway product sales rather than high-margin recurring service revenue, creating risk that the commercial ramp delivers lower economics than the long-run model assumes.

Share count continues to grow (285M → 300M Class A in six months) via RSU vesting, equity distributions, and stock compensation ($123M H1 2026), which is a real and ongoing cost to existing shareholders.
